Pain radiates to the groin, comes in waves
Serum Ca normal; 24-h urine calcium high, citrate low
Noncontrast CT: 5-mm radiopaque distal ureteral stone
dx.e: ~70% of stones; prevent with fluids, thiazide, citrate, normal dietary Ca.

clues: Spinal cord injury with neurogenic bladder
CT: branching stone filling the renal pelvis
dx.e: Urease → alkaline urine → magnesium ammonium phosphate.
Defective dibasic amino acid transport; alkalinize with K citrate.

clues: CT: enhancing renal mass invading the renal vein; cells clear
dx.e: VHL/3p loss; paraneoplastic EPO.

clues: 3-year-old with an abdominal mass found by mother at bath
Smooth flank mass not crossing midline
Biopsy: blastema, epithelial and stromal elements
dx.e: WAGR (WT1 deletion 11p13).

clues: 30-year-old woman with sudden flank pain and hypotension
CT: fat-containing renal mass with hemorrhage
dx.e: Tuberous sclerosis association; bleeding risk when large.

clues: 58-year-old with a 5-cm renal mass found on CT done for back strain
Asymptomatic; never smoked; no family history
Mahogany-brown tumor with central stellate scar; eosinophilic cells packed with mitochondria
dx.e: Benign; may mimic chromophobe RCC.

clues: 40 pack-years; worked in a dye factory
Cystoscopy: papillary mass; biopsy invades muscularis propria
dx.e: Smoking, aryl amines; muscle-invasive = T2+.

dx.dx: Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder
clues: Years of terminal hematuria since childhood
dx.e: S. haematobium → squamous metaplasia → SCC.

clues: Ate undercooked hamburger at a party
dx.e: Supportive care; plasma exchange not effective.

clues: Platelets 15,000, schistocytes, LDH high, Coombs negative
dx.e: Plasma exchange + immunosuppression ± caplacizumab.

clues: 45-year-old with severe headache and blurred vision
Biopsy: onion-skin arterioles, fibrinoid necrosis; flea-bitten kidney
dx.e: Hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis.
FMD in young women; atherosclerosis in older men.

clues: 50-year-old with skin thickening of hands and face
Diffuse systemic sclerosis diagnosed 1 year ago
dx.e: Treat with ACE inhibitor.

clues: Weak stream and nocturia for years
dx.e: Relieve with catheter; watch for postobstructive diuresis.

clues: Newborn boy with poor urinary stream
VCUG: dilated posterior urethra; bilateral hydronephrosis
dx.e: Most common cause of bilateral hydronephrosis in boys.
Looks like thiazide use.
ENaC gain of function.

clues: Biopsy: collapsing FSGS with tubular microcysts
dx.e: Collapsing variant; APOL1.

clues: 55-year-old woman with flank pain and passing tissue in urine
Daily analgesic mixtures for chronic headaches for years
dx.e: Analgesics, DM, sickle cell, obstruction.

clues: Phosphate high, Ca low, PTH very high, FGF-23 high
dx.e: Secondary hyperparathyroidism.

clues: Two days of dysuria and frequency
Urine microscopy: numerous white cells and gram-positive cocci in clusters
dx.e: The novobiocin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococcus with a predilection for young sexually active women.

clues: 68-year-old woman seen for a routine review
No dysuria, frequency, flank pain or fever
A second specimen two weeks later grows the same organism at the same count
She feels entirely well between the two visits
dx.e: Two consecutive voided specimens at 10⁵ CFU/mL in a woman without symptoms; pyuria does not change the definition.

clues: Indwelling urinary catheter for three weeks
Afebrile, no suprapubic or flank tenderness
Culture: Candida albicans; blood cultures negative
dx.e: Yeast in the urine of a catheterised diabetic patient is usually colonisation rather than infection.

clues: Months of frequency and intermittent flank ache
Urinalysis: pyuria with an acid urine
Routine bacterial cultures are repeatedly sterile
Acid-fast bacilli grow only after large-volume specimens are sent on three mornings
dx.e: Sterile pyuria with a chronic course; the organism is hard to recover unless volume and repeat specimens are requested.

clues: 46-year-old man five months after kidney transplantation
Creatinine rising slowly without fever or graft tenderness
Urine: decoy cells, no bacterial growth
Plasma viral load high for a small naked DNA virus
Graft biopsy: tubular injury with viral inclusions
dx.e: A benign childhood virus that persists latently in the kidney and causes graft disease under immunosuppression.

clues: 9-year-old boy three weeks after a stem-cell transplant
Sudden frequency, dysuria and visible blood in the urine
Urine: red cells too numerous to count, no casts
PCR detects a naked DNA virus, type 11
dx.e: Types 11 and 21 (also 34 and 35) cause haemorrhagic cystitis in children and immunocompromised patients.
